messages:
jin: quick heads-up — I'm kicking off a bring-up for judge-v3-quant (4-bit) against the eval-harness. want to surface signal coverage and tie-break behaviour before we flip it into CI.
sasha: awesome. what's the primary worry? regression on sensitive slices or flakiness from quant noise?
jin: both. quant noise is causing more pairwise flips than expected. also runner is throwing occasional OOMs when we enable dense batching for long contexts.
tyler: OOMs = runner bug or config? can you paste the command you used?
jin: `./eval-runner --model judge-v3-quant --batch 64 --seq-len 2048 --cache-prefixing on --slices demographic,topic,style`
priya: batch 64 with seq 2048 on 4-bit seems aggressive. try batch 16 to isolate. also we should log KV cache mem usage.
jin: yup stepping down to 16 for isolation. splitting runs: coverage grid = [age_group, region, prompt_type], sample size 10k per cell.
alex: for tie-breaker, we need a deterministic policy. proposal: primary judge (model score), secondary is meta-judge consensus (ensemble of 3 smaller judges), final fallback = random seeded by example id. keeps reproducible while preventing endless ties.
mari: +1 for seeded fallback, but prefer weighted consensus instead of simple majority. calibrated weights from dev holdout to minimize false positives on bias slices.
sasha: how are we defining bias slices and metrics? we need per-slice delta against anchor baseline and bootstrap CIs. if delta > threshold AND p<0.05 then flag.
priya: metrics list: pairwise accuracy, agreement rate (Kripp alpha-ish), calibration gap, false positive lift on protected slices. add median logit margin for confidence proxy.
jin: noted. will compute bootstrap CI (10k resamples) and output per-slice table. planning CSV schema: `example_id, slice, anchor_decision, judge_decision, judge_score, margin, bootstrap_p`
tyler: CI wiring note: the runner currently fails to upload per-run artifacts >50MB to artifact-store. large CSVs truncated. either chunk uploads or push compressed artifacts.
alex: we should also add an aggregated dashboard card in console: per-model confusion heatmap across slices + time-series of flip-rate post-quantization.
mari: for reporting, add a 'sensitivity report' that lists top 10 prompts where judge-flip changed vs anchor and shows diff tokens. that'll help QA.
sasha: quick experiment suggestion: A/B the tie-break strategies on a small holdout (50k examples) and compute acceptance delta and slice-lift. run both with identical random seeds.
jin: launching experiments: 1) batch=16 vs 64 to debug runner OOMs, 2) tie-breaker: majority vs weighted-ensemble vs seeded-fallback, 3) quantized vs fp16 judge.
priya: volunteers? I can own the slice-definition and bootstrap scripts. alex can do dashboard panels. sasha and tyler pair on runner/CI fixes. jin you own orchestration and run artifacts.
jin: sounds good. I'll push a small RFC snippet in /docs but for now dumping run matrix here. will attach logs when finishes.
eval-bot: CI: eval-runner job started for thread 2418009999. job_id=ev-8291. status=running. artifacts will be uploaded to s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/ev-8291/.
alex: one more; add a metric to capture judge sensitivity to prompt prefixing (prefix flip-rate). quant tends to change low-margin examples. helps explain edge-case diffs.
mari: ok let's sync tomorrow 10am PT to triage results and decide rollout gating criteria. agenda: regression thresholds, tie-break policy, dashboard mockups.
jin: thanks all — running now, will post intermediate logs in thread. :thumbsup:
